Q1: Which branch should the fix be planned and implemented against?
Choices:
A. PR #6999's head branch `ai/issue-6987`, where the failing assertion was introduced. Add `Target branch: ai/issue-6987` to the plan context so the fix stacks onto that PR. (RECOMMENDED)
B. The default branch `main`. On `main` the cited assertion is not present, so this would most likely produce no changes.
C. No separate fix. Close this issue and let PR #6999's own review/autofix loop repair its test.
Q2: If reproducing the shard shows a different cause from the one the triage guessed, how far may the fix go?
Choices:
A. Fix whichever side is wrong, test or `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh`, using the documented behaviour. The waiver records the finding's actual `exploit_scenario` (`scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:7156-7170`, agents.md waiver matching), so a test that expects a different scenario is the side to change. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Change only `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py`. If the cause turns out to be in the script, emit BLOCKED.
C. Change only the single assertion the triage suggested, even if the shard still fails afterwards.
